paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: We introduce a new framework called Self-Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation (SELF -RAG) that enhances an LM’s quality and factuality through retrieval and self-reflection.
review_rationale: Supported by the framework description and Figure 1; Self-RAG combines retrieval with self-reflection.
annotation_note: Keep as method claim; do not treat as a quantified performance result.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: Our framework trains a single arbitrary LM that adaptively retrieves passages on-demand, and generates and reflects on retrieved passages and its own generations using special tokens, called reflection tokens.
review_rationale: Supported: one LM is trained to retrieve on demand and generate/reflect using special reflection tokens.
annotation_note: Clarify that retrieval is conditional and reflection tokens guide generation.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: Generating reflection tokens makes the LM controllable during the inference phase, enabling it to tailor its behavior to diverse task requirements.
review_rationale: Supported as a design capability; controllability is described through reflection tokens and decoding controls.
annotation_note: Avoid implying user-controllability is independently evaluated across all possible tasks.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: Experiments show that SELF RAG (7B and 13B parameters) significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs and retrieval-augmented models on a diverse set of tasks.
review_rationale: The abstract-level claim that it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art systems across a diverse set of tasks is too broad without specifying task, comparator, and metric.
annotation_note: Use the task-specific quantitative comparisons instead; see P019-CORR-01 and P019-CORR-02.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: Specifically, SELF -RAG outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on Open-domain QA, reasoning and fact verification tasks, and it shows significant gains in improving factuality and citation accuracy for long-form generations relative to these models.1 1 I NTRODUCTION State-of-the-art LLMs continue to struggle with factual errors (Mallen et al., 2023; Min et al., 2023) despite their increased model and data scale (Ouyang et al., 2022).
review_rationale: The comparison is task- and metric-dependent. ASQA citation precision improves for Self-RAG, but recall does not beat retrieval-augmented ChatGPT; avoid blanket superiority.
annotation_note: Use task-specific claims; P019-CORR-02 preserves the exact ASQA metrics.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: Empirical results on six tasks, including reasoning and long-form generation, demonstrate that SELFRAG significantly outperforms pre-trained and instruction-tuned LLMs that have more parameters and widely adopted RAG approaches with higher citation accuracy.
review_rationale: Six-task summary is a broad synthesis; superiority varies by task, baseline, and metric.
annotation_note: Do not treat as universal superiority. Retain only as a qualified narrative summary if needed.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: The critic achieves a higher than 90% agreement with GPT-4-based predictions on most reflection token categories (Appendix Table 5).
review_rationale: The critic agreement is reported as >90% against GPT-4-generated predictions for most reflection-token categories.
annotation_note: Comparison target is GPT-4 predictions, not human annotation. Use P019-CORR-03.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: Our approach also significantly outperforms a concurrent method that employs sophisticated prompt engineering; specifically, on the bio generation task, our 7B and 13B models outperform the concurrent CoVE (Dhuliawala et al., 2023), which iteratively prompts Llama265B to refine output.
review_rationale: The paper reports comparison with CoVe on biography generation, but the statement is narrow to that task and setup.
annotation_note: Keep the scope tied to biography generation; do not generalize to all generation tasks.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: On ASQA, our model shows significantly higher citation precision and recall than all models except ChatGPT.
review_rationale: ASQA citation precision/recall comparison is not uniformly better than ChatGPT; ChatGPT retains higher recall.
annotation_note: Replace with exact values in P019-CORR-02.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_claim: Our holistic evaluations on six tasks using multiple metrics demonstrate that SELF-RAG significantly outperforms LLMs with more parameters or with conventional retrieval-augmented generation approaches.
review_rationale: This repeats the broad six-task superiority claim and obscures task-level variation.
annotation_note: Merge into a qualified synthesis or replace with task-specific results.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_claim: We therefore present Q ASPER , a dataset of 5,049 questions over 1,585 Natural Language Processing papers.
review_rationale: Supported: QASPER contains 5,049 questions over 1,585 NLP papers.
annotation_note: Keep exact counts; see also P020-CORR-01 for richer dataset statistics.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_claim: Each question is written by an NLP practitioner who read only the title and abstract of the corresponding paper, and the question seeks information present in the full text.
review_rationale: Supported: question writers saw title and abstract; questions target information in the full text.
annotation_note: Question writers and answer annotators are separate groups.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_claim: The questions are then answered by a separate set of NLP practitioners who also provide supporting evidence to answers.
review_rationale: Supported: separate NLP practitioners answer questions and provide evidence snippets.
annotation_note: Evidence can include text, tables, or figures.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_claim: We ﬁnd that existing models that do well on other QA tasks do not perform well on answering these questions, underperforming humans by at least 27F1 points when answering them from entire papers, motivating further research in document-grounded, information-seeking QA, which our dataset is designed to facilitate.
review_rationale: Supported: full-paper QA systems underperform the human lower bound by at least 27 F1 points in the reported setup.
annotation_note: Specify the benchmark/model setting; do not imply all QA models or tasks.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_claim: Note that given the disagreements among the workers estimated in Section 3, this is a lower bound on human performance for two reasons: ﬁrst, because only two annotations are used to compute the metric, while systems are evaluated against all three; and second, because the annotators are NLP practitioners, not expert researchers, and it is likely that an expert would score higher.
review_rationale: Supported methodological caveat: human performance is a lower bound because only two annotations are used for metric computation and annotators are not expert researchers.
annotation_note: This is an evaluation limitation, not a model-performance result.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_claim: We note Lacks domain knowledge errors are not always solved by better entity type resolution (see †). results show plenty of room for improvement when compared to the estimated human performance, and suggest that QASPER could serve as a test-bed for evaluating document-grounded QA research.
review_rationale: The extracted sentence combines an error-category fragment with unrelated prose and does not form a reliable standalone empirical claim.
annotation_note: Do not use this row. Use well-formed, table-grounded claims instead.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: Materials and Methods: We developed CliVER, an end-to-end scientific Claim VERification system that leverages retrieval-augmented techni ques to automatically retrieve relevant clinical trial abstracts, extract pertinent sentences, and use the PICO framework to support or refute a scientific claim.
review_rationale: Supported: CliVER retrieves clinical-trial abstracts, selects rationale sentences, and uses PICO framing for claim verification.
annotation_note: Transfer-only clinical application, not a core general-AI benchmark.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: We also created an ensemble of three state-of-the-art deep learning models to classify rationale of support, refute, and neutral.
review_rationale: Supported: label prediction uses an ensemble of two BERT-based models and one prompt-based model.
annotation_note: Describe model composition precisely; avoid saying all three are deep-learning models.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: We then constructed CoVERt, a new COVID VERification dataset comprising 15 PICO-encoded drug claims accompanied by 96 manually selected and labeled clinical trial abstracts that either support or refute each claim.
review_rationale: Supported: CoVERt comprises 15 PICO-encoded COVID-19 drug claims and 96 manually selected clinical-trial abstracts.
annotation_note: Keep the scope explicitly COVID-19/clinical.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: We used CoVERt and SciFact (a public scientific claim verifi cation dataset) to assess CliVER’s performance in predicting labels.
review_rationale: Supported: CliVER is evaluated using SciFact and CoVERt for label prediction.
annotation_note: Distinguish dataset label-prediction evaluation from clinician review.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: Results: In the evaluation of label prediction accuracy on CoVERt, CliVER achieved a notable F1 score of 0.92, highlighting the efficacy of the retrieval-augmented models.
review_rationale: Supported: CoVERt label-prediction macro-F1 is 0.92 for the ensemble in the reported evaluation.
annotation_note: Do not generalize this score to end-to-end real-world performance.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: The ensemble model outperforms each individual state-of-the-art model by an absolute increase from 3% to 11% in the F1 score.
review_rationale: Supported: ensemble improves over individual models by absolute F1 gains in the reported range; dataset and setup must be stated.
annotation_note: Use exact dataset-specific comparisons from P021-CORR-02.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: Moreover, when compared with four clinicians, CliVER achieved a precision of 79.0% for abstract retrieval, 67.4% for sentence selection, and 63.2% for label prediction, respectively.
review_rationale: The three figures refer to different pipeline stages and should not all be labeled precision; abstract retrieval is reported as accuracy, sentence selection and label prediction use reviewer agreement/accuracy measures.
annotation_note: Use P021-CORR-03 with stage-specific metric wording.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: Conclusion: CliVER demonstrates its early potential to automate scientific claim verification using retrieval-augmented strategies to harness the wealth of clinical trial abstracts in PubMed.
review_rationale: Supported as the authors’ conclusion about early potential, not proof of general-purpose scientific verification.
annotation_note: Keep clearly attributed to this clinical PubMed setting.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: We observed that the ensemble of two deep language models and one prompt-based model improves the verification accuracy of each model by an absolute increase in the F1 score from 3% to 11% on CoVERt.
review_rationale: Duplicates the ensemble-improvement claim in P021-C06 and adds no independent evidence.
annotation_note: Merge into P021-CORR-02, retaining dataset-specific F1 values.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: To improve verification accuracy in the clinical domain, we introduce a new Covid VERification dataset (CoVERt).
review_rationale: The rationale for CoVERt is described, but the wording is too generic to stand as a substantive empirical finding.
annotation_note: Use P021-CORR-01 for dataset composition and counts.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: Supplementary Table S3 shows that the Majority Voting ensemble achieved the best perform­ ance with a macro-average F1 score of 0.85.
review_rationale: Supplementary Table S3 is cited for the end-to-end sentence-selection-plus-labeling evaluation; majority-voting ensemble macro-F1 is 0.85.
annotation_note: Do not confuse this with the 0.92 oracle label-prediction score. See P021-CORR-04.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: For the Neutral class, we observed a higher precision of 1.0 and a lower recall of 0.89 on CoVERt compared to those on the SciFact dataset.
review_rationale: Supported: CoVERt neutral class precision is 1.0 and recall is 0.89; comparison is with SciFact neutral-class performance.
annotation_note: Class-specific result; not an overall model score.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_claim: We observed that the majority voting ensemble model achieved the best performance when claims were formatted using Template 2, with a macro-average F1 score of 0.93.
review_rationale: Supported: Template 2 yields the best reported majority-voting result, macro-F1 0.93, in the claim-variation experiment.
annotation_note: Keep tied to the template-variation experiment, not the main benchmark result.
